rows.construct: Extension elements and attributes in other namespaces (`Selection`, `Ordering`, `CustomOperator`, `CustomInteraction`, `CompanionMaterialsInfo`; strict or lax)
Item session states initial, interacting, suspended, closed, review, solution and their transitions
RR session status from session state: initial, pendingSubmission, pendingResponseProcessing, pendingExternalScoring, final
`numAttempts` 0 at start, +1 at the start of each attempt
Item `duration` from `at` timestamps: candidate sessions summed, suspended time excluded, truncated to 0.001 s resolution
`completionStatus` not_attempted → unknown at first attempt; set by response processing; adaptive `completed` closes the session
Response variables NULL at start; declared default applied at the start of the first attempt; never applied when never attempted
Outcome initial value: declared default, else 0 for integer and float, else NULL

Non-adaptive items: outcomes reset to defaults before each response processing; with one attempt the first outcomes are reported; when item session control allows more attempts, the last outcomes are reported
Adaptive items: outcomes kept between attempts; last outcomes reported; `max-attempts` ignored

End attempt interaction: its response is true when it ended the attempt, false otherwise; its default is ignored; with `count-attempt="false"` the attempt it ends is left out of the `max-attempts` budget while `numAttempts` still increments; absent means true (D8)
Template processing once at session start; `qti-template-constraint` restarts processing with defaults until true, at most 100 times, then keeps defaults

Operator attributes as variable references: integer and float unions take a bare identifier; `pattern` takes `{identifier}` and is literal when no such variable exists; `n` and `number-repeats` take an identifier
Choice visibility through `template-identifier` and `show-hide` on choices, hotspots, gaps, hottext
Feedback, template block and inline visibility: shown when `show-hide="show"` and the variable matches or contains the identifier; inverted for `hide`

Integrated feedback and review: feedback after the last attempt only when `show-feedback`; review state only when `allow-review`; for non-adaptive items the review shows the body as at attempt start; for adaptive items `show-feedback` is ignored when `allow-review` is true and review uses the final outcomes
Modal feedback shown directly after response processing
Test feedback `during` after outcome processing, `atEnd` at the end of its part or test
Rubric blocks by `view`; section rubric concatenated from the top section down; no interactions; no nesting

Printed variable: C `printf` conversions `E e f G g r R i o X x` with flags, width, precision; `i` in `base`; `index`, `field`, `delimiter` (`;`), `mapping-indicator` (`=`), `power-form`; response variables not printable
Selection without replacement: `select` children, every `required` child included, a sub-section counts as one; fewer than required is an error
Selection with replacement: children eligible more than once; `select` may exceed the child count
Ordering: `shuffle` permutes children; `fixed` children keep their positions, fixed after selection
`visible` sections; invisible sections in a shuffled parent shuffle as a block when `keep-together`, else their children mix with the parent's
`qti-assessment-section-ref` resolved by href to a section document
Navigation: linear parts move forward only; non-linear parts allow any item

Submission: individual per item; simultaneous at the end of the part, one attempt, no feedback during the test; adaptive items incompatible with simultaneous; except that items of adaptive sections in a simultaneous part get response and outcome processing per item before Submit Results (CAT §2.4)
Pre-conditions in order, linear parts only, skip the item, section or part when one is false; test parts may have them
Branch rules after presentation; target forward in the same part, or another part; `EXIT_SECTION`, `EXIT_TESTPART`, `EXIT_TEST`; ignored in non-linear parts; paths are trees
Item session control inheritance: test part, then sections, then item reference, each overriding
`max-attempts`: unspecified is 1 for non-adaptive items, 0 is unlimited, more than 1 requires feedback between attempts

`allow-skipping`: a skip is a submission with only default or NULL responses; enforced in individual mode only; an item without response variables is never considered skipped, so `allow-skipping="false"` never blocks it
`validate-responses`: submission refused until every interaction's response is valid; individual mode only
`allow-review`, `show-feedback`, `show-solution`, `allow-comment` gate review, feedback, solution and comment actions
Time limits `min-time`, `max-time`, `allow-late-submission` at item, section, part and test; minimum only in linear mode for items and sections; part and test time include navigation
PNP additional testing time: `time-multiplier` scales every maximum time, `fixed-minutes` extends the outermost maximum, `unlimited` removes maximum times; minimum times unchanged (G41)
Outcome processing after each submission (individual) or group (simultaneous), after response processing; test outcomes reset to defaults before each run

Item variable lookup `ITEM.VAR` and `ITEM.n.VAR` for with-replacement instances; last submitted instance in simultaneous mode (else per G9); response variables give the last submitted value, never drafts (B96)
Weights: `weight-identifier` scales numeric item variables, missing weight is 1.0, result float
Variable mappings rename item outcomes for the test
Template defaults from the test override item template defaults before template processing

`outcome-minimum` ignores items without a minimum; `outcome-maximum` is NULL if any item lacks a maximum; `test-variables` skips NULLs and, with `base-type`, matches only variables of that base type; integer unless any float; a weight is defined only with `base-type` float or omitted (weight with integer is a validate error)

Response processing templates: the six RPT files are built in as model constants; URIs are normalized (`.xml` optional, `http` or `https`, `purl.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/rptemplates/` or `www.imsglobal.org/question/qti_v3p0/rptemplates/`); QTI 2.x template URIs map to the same three algorithms with a validate warning (G43); internal rules win when both are given; `template-location` through the resolver
Conditions: a NULL or false condition skips its branch
Assignment checks base type and cardinality against the declaration, with promotion per D5

`lookup-outcome-value`: interpolation table takes the first entry whose `source-value` ≤ value (strict when `include-boundary` is false); match table takes the exact integer; otherwise `default-value` or NULL
Context declarations in items and tests; delivery engine supplies values before processing
Identifier syntax: letter or `_` first; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`; period reserved for prefixes; case-sensitive; 32 characters recommended
Response binding per interaction: base type and cardinality allowed for each of the 23 interactions
Text and extended text: record fields `stringValue`, `floatValue`, `integerValue`, `leftDigits`, `rightDigits`, `ndp`, `nsf`, `exponent`; `string-identifier` keeps the raw text; `base`
Order interaction: a default value overrides the initial order
Choice interaction starts with nothing selected; hottext starts from the default value

Interaction constraints for validity: min/max choices, associations, strings, `match-min`/`match-max` (0 is unlimited), `required`, `pattern-mask`, slider bounds and step, media plays, upload MIME types
Choice shuffling: `shuffle` randomizes initial order, `fixed` choices keep their positions, each match set shuffles separately
Solution state replaces responses with correct responses, or NULL
Clones: a clone gets its own identifier and records template values; reports convert back to the template
Item and test fragments through XInclude where the XSD allows `xi:include` (42 types), as parsed XML, without xpointer
External scoring: `external-scored` (human, externalMachine), `variable-identifier-ref`; session waits in pendingExternalScoring until scores applied
Shared stimulus through `qti-assessment-stimulus-ref` and package dependencies
Companion materials (calculator, rule, protractor, digital and physical materials) as data
Custom operators: dispatch to a registered function by `definition`, else `class`; unregistered is a ProcessingError (G7)
Custom interaction (deprecated): data kept; response binding unchecked

Adaptive section (CAT): `qti-adaptive-selection` excludes `qti-selection` and `qti-ordering`; no nested sections; top-level only; branch rules and pre-conditions on its items, and branch rules targeting its items, are ignored; stages appended in order
CAT item flow: response and outcome processing before Submit Results; CAT outcome values merged into results; results per presented item with `sequenceIndex`, skipped items `initial`
Catalogs: one card per support in a catalog; card or card entry has HTML content or file references; card entry chosen by `xml:lang`, else `default`
PNP sets: activate as option, activate at initialization, prohibit; a prohibited support is not assigned
Answered status from validity: answered, attempted, presented, notpresented
Math operators: domains give NULL; reciprocal and `atan2` rules; `signum`, `floor`, `ceil` integer results
Rounding: `round` to n for [n − 0.5, n + 0.5); `truncate` toward zero; NaN gives NULL; `round`, `truncate`, `floor`, `ceil` of ±INF give NULL (D4)
`round-to` and `equal-rounded` by the deciding digit of the decimal representation, significant figures ≥ 1, decimal places ≥ 0
Division by zero and results outside the float range give NULL (`divide`, `power`)
`equal` tolerance: exact, absolute [x − t0, x + t1], relative [x(1 − t0/100), x(1 + t1/100)], bound inclusion flags
`map-response`: single maps one value; containers sum distinct values once; `default-value` for unmapped keys; bounds; `case-sensitive` keys default false
`map-response-point`: areas tested in order, each area counted once; bounds
Shapes and coordinates for `inside` and area maps: circle, rect, poly, ellipse, default; percentages
`pattern-match` in XML Schema regex syntax, matching the whole string
`stats-operator`: mean; sample and population variance and SD require more than one value

Integer arithmetic: `integer-divide` floors, `integer-modulus` is x − z·y, zero divisor gives NULL; `gcd`/`lcm` zero rules; `sum`, `product`, `min`, `max`, `subtract` integer only when all operands are
Containers: `multiple` and `ordered` flatten and drop NULLs; `repeat`; `index` from 1; `random`; `container-size` of NULL is 0; `delete`; `member`; `contains` (multiset or subsequence)
`correct` and `default` look up declarations, with item prefixes in outcome processing
`match` compares equal values (pair unordered); should not be used for float, must not for duration
Outcome-only expressions are errors in response processing: `outcome-minimum`, `outcome-maximum`, `test-variables` (BIND rule set), and the `number-*` expressions (INFO "only in outcomes processing")
End of attempt only on a candidate action or an expected event, such as the end of the test

Package rules: one resource per item, section, test, stimulus; single-item packages put metadata on the resource; `cp:organization` and `cp:item` prohibited; schema and version values; auxiliary files listed or shared through dependencies
Variants: `cpx:variant` on the core item's resource, with DRD metadata
Separate outcome declaration and response processing template resources, linked by dependencies
CAT configuration files listed in the manifest when package-relative
Relative hrefs resolve against the referencing file and `xml:base`; references outside the package are reported
XXE, SSRF and path traversal controls of §2.6
Adaptive items in review: final outcomes decide integrated feedback; `show-feedback` ignored when `allow-review` is true
Draft and submitted responses are kept apart: expressions, outcome processing and results `final` read the last submitted values; RR `pendingSubmission` snapshots the drafts
A branch rule must not target an item that selection with replacement can repeat
In non-linear parts with adaptive sections, results for earlier items may be sent again in a later Submit Results

Hazard terms: DRD `flashing`, `sound`, `olfactoryHazard`, `motionSimulation` map to PNP `hazard-avoidance` `flashing`, `sound`, `olfactory-hazard`, `motion-simulation`; candidates who avoid a hazard should not be exposed to content with it

Variant selection, by the engine at the first presentation of an item instance, fixed for the session: candidates are the core item and its `cpx:variant`s; drop every candidate whose DRD hazards the PNP avoids (B99); among the rest prefer the variant whose DRD `languageOfAdaptation` matches the PNP `item-translation` language (exact tag, then primary subtag), else the core item; if every candidate is dropped, deliver the core item with its hazards flagged `avoided` and emit `hazard-unavoidable`. The choice is stored and emitted as `variant-selected`; results keep the item ref identifier (RR §2.4.5). Switching variants during a session is out of scope for 1.0

`metadata` (manifest): `schema` ∈ {QTI Package, QTI Item Bank, QTI Test Bank, QTI Object Bank, QTI Test, QTI Section, QTI Item}, `schemaversion` = `3.0.0`, `lom:lom`, `csmd:curriculumStandardsMetadataSet`
PNP files must not be in a package; results files must not be in a package
Vocabulary ObjectTypeEnum: test, testpart, section, item, outcome, interaction, choice
External vocabulary Distractor Statistics: AISResponse, NumberChoosingResponse, PTbis-Response, PercentChoosingResponse

External vocabulary Item Statistics: A-Param, AIS, B-Param, C-Param, D-Param, Fifths_Table_{Highest, Second_Highest, Middle, Second_Lowest, Lowest}, P-value, PHI, PTbis, Polyserial, Score_Conversion, rbis
Usage data as CAT pool input (`qti-usagedata-ref`)
Vocabulary AnsweredStatusEnum: answered, attempted, presented, notpresented
Vocabulary AssignmentEnum: assigned, inherit, prohibited, universal
Create Section `POST {prefix}/sections` with Section Data; returns `sectionIdentifier`
Get Section `GET {prefix}/sections/{id}`; returns Section Data and the pool as an Item Stage
Create Session `POST …/sessions` with PNP (base64), demographics, prior data; returns the first stage and `sessionState`
Submit Results `POST …/sessions/{id}/results`; returns CAT outcomes, next stage, `sessionState`
Section Data: `sectionConfiguration`, `qtiUsagedata`, `qtiMetadata` (base64 of the referenced files)
Item Stage: `itemIdentifiers`, `stageLength`; presented in order; repeats instanced as with replacement; empty means session end
Assessment Result in the REST/JSON binding (`context`, `testResult`, `itemResult`)

Minimal results report: SCORE (float, single) per responded item, `duration`, `numAttempts`, `completionStatus`; skipped items `initial`, unpresented items excluded or `sequenceIndex` 0; in simultaneous parts the items still get response and outcome processing before the request (B27)

JSON binding of single values `{ "base":  { "<type>":  … } }`, NULL `{ "base":  null }`; duration as ISO 8601; file `{ data, mime, name }` converted to and from references through host callbacks; `intOrIdentifier` (G38)
JSON binding of multiple and ordered values `{ "list":  { "<type>":  […] } }`
JSON binding of records `{ "record":  [ { "name", "base" } ] }`; a field may be `"base":  null` (G37)
Module resolution file: JSON with `waitSeconds` (default 7, 0 = no timeout) and `paths` (no `.js` extension; protocol means absolute, else package-relative)
`module` attribute or `qti-interaction-modules` must name a configured module; per-module `primary-path` and `fallback-path`

`data-*` attributes passed as properties; template and context variables passed through `qti-template-variable`, `qti-context-variable`; `qti-interaction-markup`; the PCI's opaque state stored with the session and returned for `getInstance` (E29)
Package-relative module files listed in the manifest
PCI JavaScript API, AMD loading, timeouts, fallback switching
Engine as a pure reducer: `apply(state, action)` returns a new state and events, or a refusal; no I/O, timers or clock reads
Serializable, versioned state: plain data with values as `WireValue` (E30); file values are references (D7); PCI states, supports and variant choices included
Explicit seed; generator state stored in the session; replaying the action log from the seed reproduces the state exactly
Refusal values `{ code, message, source }` for disallowed actions; a refusal leaves the state unchanged
Every action carries `at` (epoch milliseconds). `stamp(state, action, now)` uses `max(now, last at)`, so server clock skew never refuses; only unstamped device logs can hit `clock-regression` (G27)
Deadlines the host can query: maximum and minimum times per item, section, part and test, as absolute times, PNP-adjusted, suspended time excluded

Time-out: a `time` action, or any action at or after a deadline, first applies it. Without `allow-late-submission`: open attempts in the scope end with the responses received before the deadline, the scope closes, navigation moves on, later actions in it are refused `time-over`. With it: the deadline emits `time-limit-passed` and does not close the scope; later submissions are accepted with a `late-submission` event (RR has no flag) until the candidate or host ends the scope (D9). `view(state, now)` shows a passed deadline as applied, by the same logic
Suspend and resume of the whole session; item sessions pass to suspended; suspended time counts nowhere (G23)
Navigation, submission modes, pre-conditions, branch rules, selection and ordering applied as the candidate moves
Adaptive items: repeated attempts, outcomes kept, completion ends the session
Item instances keyed `{ ref, instance }` (with-replacement selections and CAT repeats)

Standalone item delivery for practice: a one-item, non-linear, individual-submission session; without a given control, feedback and review are shown (`show-feedback` and `allow-review` true) and adaptive rules apply, because the item session control defaults are stated for a test context

Pending external scoring: one request per external-scored outcome: item-level when its item session closes, test-level when every covered instance is closed or the test ends (G26); covers that were never presented are listed with `presented: false`
Requests carry the outcome declaration, mode (human or externalMachine), `variable-identifier-ref`, and the covered responses (exact strings, B96) with labels

`supply-scores`: one value for the request's outcome, checked against the declaration (refusal `score-type-mismatch`); accepted in any state while the request exists, also after the test ended; a second supply replaces the value (`scores-replaced`); test outcome processing re-runs; item response processing does not (G25)
An external-scored test outcome's supplied value is its reset value for every later outcome processing run (G24); until supplied, its declared default
Outcomes and results provisional while requests are pending: item `pendingExternalScoring`, `scoreStatus="notscored"`; final when none remain

Adaptive sections: create-session request on entry; submit-results per the C4 policy after response and outcome processing of the stage's items (also in simultaneous parts, B27); `cat-response` action appends the stage; `drainCat` runs pending requests through a `CatPort` with an injected clock

Candidate view: test and part identity, navigation map of visible sections, current item content after resolution (feedback, template content, printed variables, hidden choices removed, choices in presentation order), interaction descriptors, draft responses, visible modal and test feedback, candidate rubric in the order test, part, sections top down, timers, allowed actions, supports with state and settings (R2), hazards (R4), PCI state (R3), LTI link data (R5)
rows.source: INFO §2.2.1, INFO §2.3.4, INFO §2.6, INFO §2.10, INFO §4.2, INFO §4.2.6, INFO §7.19

rows.construct: Candidate view never contains: response, template or outcome processing; correct responses (outside the solution state), mappings, area mappings, lookup tables; outcome declarations or values (results keep every outcome with its `view`; the candidate sees outcomes only through feedback and printed variables); template declarations or values (except those passed to a PCI by `qti-template-variable`, and context values passed by `qti-context-variable`); hidden feedback, template content or choices; rubric blocks whose `view` lacks `candidate`; metadata other than hazards
Solution state shows correct responses only when `show-solution` allows it and the item is closed

Server-authoritative mode: the client receives JSON views and sends JSON candidate actions; `parseCandidateAction` validates shape, types and size limits; the server stamps `at`; host-only actions (`time`, `supply-scores`, `cat-response`) never come from the client. Device mode: the same engine and view run locally
Events: every member of `DeliveryEventType` (§3.9), with times and identifiers, as neutral data for logging and analytics

Results assembly: always a `context`; `testResult` with test outcomes and durations; one `itemResult` per presented instance with `sequenceIndex` (INFO §5.98), a datestamp from the time of its last event (skip, time-out, submission), `sessionStatus`, response variables (`choiceSequence`, `answeredStatus`, `scoreStatus`), item `duration` even when not time dependent, outcomes with their `view`, template and context variables, comments, and `support` entries for supports used (assigned from the PNP, universal from the start options)

LTI items (R5): an item ref resolving to a `cartridge_basiclti_link` is deliverable. olah models it as an item with no response variables and two outcomes, `SCORE` and `MAXSCORE` (float, single, `external-scored="externalMachine"`); presenting it gives `CandidateItem.lti`; `submit` or leaving it closes the session and requests both outcomes (E13), which tempuh supplies from the tool's AGS `scoreGiven` and `scoreMaximum` (G42)

`createEngine` runs the static checks over every reachable item and throws `DataError` with the issues, including any `Include` left after resolution (F-m18); at run time a processing failure becomes data (outcomes at declared defaults, `pendingResponseProcessing`, `processing-failed` event); `apply` never throws on an accepted test

Scorer view (R6): the request plus the scorer rubric and, per covered item, its body as the candidate saw it after template processing with scorer-view rubric, template values, submitted responses and correct responses; server side only

Support toggles (R2): `support` action turns an `activate-as-option` support on or off; prohibited supports are refused `support-not-available`; supports active while an item is presented are recorded for its results

PCI state (R3): `set-responses` may carry opaque PCI states per response identifier (size-limited); the engine stores the latest and returns it in the view for `getInstance` on resume, also on another device
rows.source: BPIG §3.7.12, CERT App. A T-14 ("Record and Restore Responses")

rows.construct: JSON wire forms (R1): `viewToJson`/`viewFromJson`, `actionToJson`/`parseCandidateAction` and `serializeState`/`deserializeState` carry values as `WireValue` (`{ cardinality, baseType?, value }` around App. C), decodable without declarations and lossless (multiple versus ordered, typed NULL, durations as `PT<shortest decimal>S`); maps become entry arrays, never objects keyed by identifiers

Markup: a child `qti-rubric-block` of `qti-assessment-test`, after `qti-stylesheet` and before `qti-test-part` (XSD order), with `view` containing `scorer`, `use="scoring"`, class token `external-score-covers`, `data-outcome-identifier`; content: optional notes, then `ul` of `li` with `data-item-ref` and `data-response-identifier`; the label is the `li`'s text content with whitespace normalized
The block stays an ordinary `RubricBlock` in the test model (one source of truth, position and attributes kept); `readScoreCovers(test)` derives the covers keyed by outcome identifier
`scoreCoversBlock(outcome, covers, notes)` builds the block; a round trip keeps it unchanged
Covers are independent of outcome processing: they come only from blocks, never from analysis of the rules that use the outcome (sums, routing)
A test without blocks has no covers; its external-scored outcomes still produce requests, with empty covers
Error: a block for an undeclared outcome
Error: a block for an outcome that is not `external-scored`
Error: a cover naming an unknown `qti-assessment-item-ref`
Error: a cover naming a response the referenced item does not declare
Error: the same cover twice in a block, or two blocks for one outcome
Error: a block whose `view` list lacks `scorer`, or contains `candidate`; an `li` without both attributes. Warning: a block with the class token below test level (not recognized)
Engine requests carry the covers resolved to instances, presented or not, with labels and the candidate's last submitted values

References to undeclared variables: `qti-variable`, `qti-default`, `qti-correct`, `qti-map-response(-point)`, set and lookup rules, printed variables, feedback `outcome-identifier`, `template-identifier`, PCI variables, item-prefixed references
Duplicate identifiers in an item's variable namespace; duplicate test part, section and item-ref identifiers
Static operand checks: each operator's required base types and cardinalities, inferred bottom-up; custom operators and record fields are unknown and skipped
Assignment checks for set rules, lookup tables (match tables need integers), template defaults, with D5's promotion
Unreachable identifiers: feedback or template-content identifiers that the controlling variable can never take, when every assignment to it is a constant
Unreachable items, sections and parts under branch rules; unknown, backward or cyclic branch targets; targets that selection with replacement can repeat (B97)
`duration` used in an item that is not time dependent
Weights referenced but not defined on the item ref
Unknown response processing template without internal rules (G17)

`olah validate <path>`: a zip, an unpacked package directory (symlinks contained) or a single XML document (ASI, manifest, results, usage data, PNP), detected by root element; every document through `parseXml`, then the XSD checks with one compiled schema set, then all semantic checks

Output: text by default, `--format json` gives `{ tool, version, target, valid, summary: { errors, warnings }, issues: Issue[] }`; exit codes 0 valid, 1 issues with errors, 2 usage, I/O or missing schemas
`olah schemas fetch [--dir]`: downloads the files of `SCHEMA_FILES` into a cache directory and checks their SHA-256; the only network access anywhere in olah
PNP documents in the two namespaces 1EdTech's own documents use (BPIG §5, BIND §7) are read, written in the XSD namespace, and reported as errors
Rendering HTML5, MathML (MathJax), SSML and CSS; DOM; shared-vocabulary classes; layout; interaction widgets
Delivery UI: navigation controls, review and solution screens, timers on screen, companion tools (calculator, rule, protractor)
